roadmap_item: F4 — light, sky and atmosphere (R1: make the key light dominant), ring 1
state: LANDED AND MEASURED. The acceptance number as literally written is NOT met — 4 of 5 judged crops, 4 of 5 full frames, and I am reporting that as a fail rather than choosing the view that passes. Every window improved, several by 5-8x, and the reason the fifth one 'fails' is that the fix put it in shadow.
WHAT_I_COULD_NOT_DO_STATED_FIRST: THE ACCEPTANCE NUMBER I WAS GIVEN IS NOT MET, AND I AM NOT GOING TO DRESS IT AS MET. 'key_off delta >= 2x env_off delta in all five judged windows' holds at pair01 (3.476), pair02 (5.576), pair04 (4.635) and pair05 (3.561), and FAILS at pair03 (0.232). Measured on the full 1920x1080 frame instead of the sealed 512x512 crop, the same build passes pair01/02/03/05 and FAILS pair04 (1.256). So there is no single view in which all five pass, and picking the view per window would be metric-shopping. 4 of 5, twice, on two different windows.

AND THE REASON IS THAT THE ACCEPTANCE NUMBER IS ITSELF AN S59 DEFECT — IT IS MAXIMISED BY DELETING SHADOWS. `key_off` measures how much the frame changes when the key is switched off. A pixel that is IN SHADOW does not change when the key is switched off, because no key light was reaching it. pair03's judged crop is now largely cast shadow: OPEN `frames/pair03__BEFORE-revert__judged-crop.png` AND `frames/pair03__AFTER__judged-crop.png` SIDE BY SIDE — before is a uniformly lit flat olive ground with no shadow anywhere; after is a large soft cast shadow across the lower two thirds with sunlit patches. The window scores WORSE on the acceptance metric precisely because the thing F4 exists to produce arrived in it. Before, pair03 measured key 0.873 against probe 29.481, ratio 0.030, and 0.873 is BELOW the instrument's noise floor — the sun was doing nothing measurable in that window at all. After: key 2.771, probe 11.939, ratio 0.232. The ratio improved 7.7x and the metric still says fail. This is the same shape as the density score that rewarded illegibility and the camera criterion satisfied by fading the player to invisible; it arrived inside the acceptance I was handed, and I did not notice it until pair03 came back red and I opened the crop.

I DID NOT REBALANCE `dusk-canopy`, `overcast-flat` OR `storm`, SO THREE OF THE FIVE EXTERIOR RECIPES STILL CARRY THE OLD BUDGET. dusk-canopy was MEASURED and REFUSED: under noon-marsh's new multipliers the 06:00 frame went from mean luma 38.358 to 27.724 (-28%), mean chroma 22.002 to 13.112 (-40%), and full-frame p10 from 9.0 to 0.0 — the bottom tenth of the frame crushed to black. `recipeForConditions()` selects it whenever |sun elevation| < ~0.157, i.e. roughly 05:20-06:40 and 17:20-18:40, so the player will still see the old flat look in those bands. overcast-flat and storm are UNMEASURED and UNTOUCHED: an overcast sky IS the light source, so the same numbers are wrong there by construction, and I had no measurement to replace them with.

I DID NOT CAPTURE MOTION, AND ONLY ONE OF MY NINE VIEWPOINTS WAS RE-SHOT ON HARDWARE. The character directive requires motion sequences and multiple angles for visual claims. This piece has nine distinct camera setups (five judged windows at 08:00/13:00/13:00/08:00/19:30, plus dusk 06:00, deep night 01:00, overcast 13:00 and an interior), before and after at six of them, and NOT ONE MOVING FRAME. The hardware confirmation (RTX A5000, ANGLE Vulkan 1.4.312) covers pair01 only, two arms. It agrees with SwiftShader to 0.03% on the landed mean luma (64.351 hardware against 64.368 software) and 0.9% on the reverted one, which is why I did not buy four more Pods — but that is an argument, not a measurement of the other eight views on hardware.

THE `revert_day` DELETE-THE-FIX ARM CANNOT UNDO ONE HALF OF THE CHANGE, AND I ONLY KNOW HOW MUCH THAT MATTERS AT ONE WINDOW. `sky.js:944` bakes the environment probe with `sunGain: R.key * max(0.05, day)`, so raising `noon-marsh.key` to 3.00 also tripled the sun lobe INSIDE the probe texture, and no page-side arm can reach a bake. Cross-checked at pair01 where a true pre-change capture exists: `revert_day` returns mean 59.462 and chroma 25.715 against the real pre-change 59.149 and 25.071 — inside the 1.51 noise floor — but sd 32.781 against 29.899, a 9.6% miss. So `revert_day` is a validated proxy for pair02/03/04 on brightness and colour and NOT on contrast, and every sd figure quoted from a `revert_day` row carries that error.

I LOST FOUR CAPTURE RUNS AND THE PAIR04 REVERT ARM. Two runs died to `Target page, context or browser has been closed` while the box sat at 94-95% disk with 2.2 GB free; two more hit the 10-minute foreground ceiling this harness imposes and were killed mid-sweep with nothing written. `f4-verify-p04` aborted on its last arm, so pair04 has a before-key number (8.538) and NO before-env number, and its before-ratio is therefore unknown rather than estimated.

I DID NOT MEASURE THE THIRTEEN REGIONS AGAINST EACH OTHER. `RI-WLD04` M17 wants regions to remain separable, and cutting the probe cuts a term that carries the region's own hue. I measured chroma per window instead, which is a proxy and not the region-separability test.
WHAT_LANDED_IN_ONE_PARAGRAPH: Four numbers in `game/src/render/lib/lighting-recipes.js` and one line in `game/src/render/sky.js`. `noon-marsh` goes key 1.00 -> 3.00, sky 0.42 -> 0.315, fill 0.30 -> 0.225, env 1.00 -> 0.35. `night-moon` gets a new `moon: 3.60` lever and env 0.75 -> 0.195. `EXTERIOR_RIG` gains a `moon` field defaulting to 1.0, and `sky.js` multiplies the moon's intensity by it. Nothing else changed: no post-processing, no shadow fit, no AO, no material, no shader. On the five judged windows the key light went from moving the judged pixels LESS than the sky probe does — 9.31 against 19.82 at pair01, 0.87 against 29.48 at pair03, 2.64 against 4.65 at pair05 — to moving them 3.5x, 5.6x and 3.6x MORE. The frame did not get darker doing it: pair01 mean luma 59.149 -> 64.368 and mean chroma 25.071 -> 29.126.

the_acceptance_measured_on_the_landed_bu.rule_as_given: key_off mean|d|rgb >= 2.0 x env_off mean|d|rgb, in ALL FIVE judged windows
the_acceptance_measured_on_the_landed_bu.instrument: tools/visual/f2-why-forced.mjs — the instrument the brief named. Extended, not replaced: a per-arm delta BASE so a candidate's arms difference against the candidate rather than against shipped; a `key_off` arm; four preservation windows; two delete-the-fix arms; and it now writes its JSON even when the browser dies mid-sweep.
the_acceptance_measured_on_the_landed_bu.why_key_off_and_not_sun_off: Derived from `sky.js` at the deck's own hours. pair05 is 19:30, where `elev = -0.383`, `day = 0` and `recipeForConditions()` returns `night-moon`, so `sun.intensity = 2.1 * max(0.02, 0) * 0.30 = 0.0126` — READ BACK OFF THE LIVE SCENE AS 0.0126. The sun is already off at pair05; the directional key there is `this.moon` at 0.82, and `sky.js:645` sets `moon.castShadow = false`. A literal `sun_off` arm at pair05 measures nothing, and the acceptance as written was unsatisfiable there for a reason that has nothing to do with the light budget. `key_off` zeroes every directional light that is a direct child of the scene root — exactly sky.js's sun and moon, and nothing else — and is identical to `sun_off` on pairs 01-04 because the moon is at 0 by day.

judged_512x512_crops.verdict: FAIL — and see the second entry under what_i_could_not_do: this crop is now cast shadow, and 0.873 before was BELOW the noise floor

judged_512x512_crops.ratio_before: env arm lost to an aborted run

same_arms_measured_over_the_full_1920x10.why: pair03's crop is one shaded patch and pair04's crop is one sunlit patch. The full frame contains both, which is what a player actually looks at.
same_arms_measured_over_the_full_1920x10.verdict: PASS on four, FAIL on pair04 at 1.256 — a DIFFERENT window from the crop failure. There is no view in which five of five pass.

noise_floors_on_the_landed_build.how: `shipped_recheck` — the shipped configuration re-captured from an unmoved camera after the other arms, so it carries the sim drift of the whole sweep

the_preservation_clause_named_before_the.why_it_exists: Ruling S59. `sun_dominant` in the diagnosis is the warning: it made the key dominant and produced a picture that was 9.4% DARKER and flatter than shipped. An acceptance that names only the ratio is satisfied by turning the ambient off.

P1_the_game_must_not_get_darker.broken_at_one_window_and_on_purpose: pair03 57.896 -> 39.901 (0.689x). It is 31% darker because a building's shadow now falls across it. Open the two crops; the darkening is shaped, not crushed.

P2_the_sky_must_not_read_as_black.held: The sky dome is untouched — no arm and no recipe field in this change reaches `uZenith`/`uHorizon`. Visible and blue in every after-frame, including on hardware.

P3_night_must_not_break.held: `RI-WLD04` M17 step 6 — a frame a judge cannot classify is a missing frame. 19:30: 28.386 -> 29.079 mean luma, sd 29.172 -> 29.108. 01:00, the darkest hour: 14.960 -> 18.660 mean luma, chroma 7.868 -> 8.302. Night got BRIGHTER and slightly more colourful, which is the direction `night-moon`'s own comment asks for.
P3_night_must_not_break.cost_paid_and_recorded: pair05's mean chroma falls 10.646 -> 9.529, a 10.5% loss. The night probe carries the region's hue and cutting it costs some of that. `night-moon` was given sky 1.05 and fill 1.00 UNCHANGED for exactly this reason — the first night candidate, which cut them to 0.75 like the day recipe, lost 16% of the chroma and still missed the ratio at 1.975.

P4_interiors_must_not_break.why_this_was_a_real_risk_and_not_a_forma: `renderer.js:1298` calls `sky.apply()` on every frame INCLUDING inside a room, and `sky.js:955` then writes `scene.environmentIntensity = R.env` from whichever EXTERIOR recipe the hour selected. So cutting noon-marsh's env from 1.00 to 0.35 lands on every interior in the game. It is survivable only because the 3x key lands there too and more than pays for it.
P4_interiors_must_not_break.and_the_crop_lied_about_it: The judged-style 512x512 crop of the same interior frame says 8.416 -> 4.549, a 46% DARKENING. It is measuring one unlit beam. The full frame is the honest number and I would not have known which to believe without opening the image.

P5_the_recipes_i_did_not_touch_must_be_b.held_exactly: prsv-dusk (06:00, dusk-canopy) measures mean 32.838, sd 24.9769, chroma 23.1565 BEFORE the change and mean 32.838, sd 24.9769, chroma 23.1565 AFTER it. Identical to four decimals — a clean null control that also happens to prove the capture is deterministic at that pose.
P5_the_recipes_i_did_not_touch_must_be_b.overcast: prsv-overcast (13:00 overcast, overcast-flat, untouched) 60.890 -> 59.328, a 2.6% difference with an unchanged recipe, i.e. sim drift. Worth noting for a different reason: BEFORE the change overcast (60.890) was BRIGHTER than clear at 08:00 (59.149), which is backwards. After it, clear at 08:00 is 64.368 against overcast 59.328 and the order is right.

P6_the_frame_must_not_get_flatter.mixed_and_reported_as_mixed: pair04, the all-terrain window, gains hugely: sd 4.180 -> 10.515, 2.5x the luma spread. pair01 loses: sd 29.899 -> 26.758 (0.895x), and pair03 41.110 -> 36.449 (0.887x).
P6_the_frame_must_not_get_flatter.why_i_do_not_treat_the_sd_losses_as_a_re: In these windows sd is mostly the ratio between bright sky and dark ground, not shaping. The diagnosis measured `sun_off` — turning the key OFF — RAISING sd from 29.899 to 32.275 while making the picture worse. A preservation clause built on sd would reward switching the sun off. The distribution tells the real story: pair01 p10 37.34 -> 44.05 and p50 45.91 -> 53.91 while p90 falls 94.81 -> 92.59, i.e. the shadows and midtones came up to meet the highlights. Mean chroma is the better witness and it rises 25.071 -> 29.126.

the_pair_that_is_the_result: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/F4-KEY-LIGHT/frames/pair03__BEFORE-revert__judged-crop.png — flat, uniformly lit ground, one olive value across the whole picture, no shadow anywhere.

corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/F4-KEY-LIGHT/frames/pair03__AFTER__judged-crop.png — the same camera, the same second: a large soft cast shadow across the lower two thirds, sunlit patches between, and the carved stonework at the back readable as stone.
on_real_hardware: hardware/pair01__BEFORE-revert__RTX-A5000.png and hardware/pair01__AFTER__RTX-A5000.png — NVIDIA RTX A5000, driver 580.159.04, ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.312), one Pod, two arms back to back in one process.

What actually changed there, stated at the strength the image supports: the roof planes separate into a sunlit slope and a shaded one where before both read the same; the walls have modelling; the stone path and the boardwalk planks show their material; the far hill has form; the ground gains a soft gradient toward the building. The DRAMATIC cast shadow is at pair03, not here — pair01's is subtle and I am not going to claim more of it than the frame shows.
the_thing_to_actually_look_at.the_refusal: frames/prsv-dusk__with-noon-marsh-numbers-REFUSED__before.png and __after.png — what 06:00 looks like if you apply these numbers to `dusk-canopy`. This is why that recipe was left alone.

a_hypothesis_i_formed_and_my_own_arm_ref.what_i_thought: That `sd_luma` in the judged window was a usable preservation metric for 'the picture must not get flatter'. The first candidate measured sd 0.878x of shipped and I nearly reported that as a regression that needed the key dialled back.
a_hypothesis_i_formed_and_my_own_arm_ref.what_the_data_said: The diagnosis's own `sun_off` row: turning the key completely OFF raises sd from 29.899 to 32.275. A metric that scores a keyless frame higher than a key-lit one is measuring the sky-to-ground ratio, not shape. Checked against the percentiles: the candidate's p10 and p50 rose 18%/17% while p90 fell 2%, which is a floor coming up, not detail being lost.
a_hypothesis_i_formed_and_my_own_arm_ref.why_this_is_recorded_rather_than_deleted: Had I acted on it I would have weakened the key to protect a number that gets better when you switch the key off — the exact S59 failure this piece was warned about, committed while writing the preservation clause meant to prevent it.

two_instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_i.1_env_off_was_killing_the_page: `env_off` was `scene.environment = null`, re-applied every frame by the enforcer. Measured three times in a row on pair01: the arm captures its own row fine and the page is dead by the NEXT arm, `Target page, context or browser has been closed` out of `stepFrames`. The identical sweep with `env_off` removed completes clean. Nulling the scene environment per frame makes three.js drop and re-derive the probe's PMREM every frame, and on SwiftShader that churn takes the page out. It is the same defect as the `fog_off` arm the diagnosis found (`scene.fog = null` poisoned the page and cost it 68 of 80 rows), in the same tool, one arm along. `env_off` is now `environmentIntensity = 0`, which three.js folds into the same `envMapIntensity` uniform. PROVEN EQUIVALENT, not assumed: the nulling form measures 19.8203 on pair01 and the intensity form measures 19.8203.
two_instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_i.2_the_interior_preservation_window_photo: The first `prsv-interior` capture returned mean 191.99, sd 5.28, and BYTE-IDENTICAL crop statistics under two different lighting configurations, with `archon-inn` written in the corner of the frame. `enterInterior` had succeeded and `whereAmI().interior` was true — but the camera was posed BEFORE the player moved into the interior cell, so it stayed at the exterior position and photographed open sky. `frame-liveness` passed it, correctly: a sky gradient is a perfectly live image. It is just not an image of a room. HAZARDS §15's second question — is the thing I am measuring in it — and the only reason it was caught is that the two arms agreeing to four decimals looked impossible and I opened the frame.

game/src/render/lib/lighting-recipes.js: EXTERIOR_RIG gains `moon: 1.0` (INTERIOR_RIG gains `moon: 0.0`), because `key` could not reach the moon and was a dead parameter at night.
night-moon: adds `moon: 3.60`, env 0.75 -> 0.195. `key`, `sky` and `fill` deliberately unchanged.
dusk-canopy: UNCHANGED, with the measurement that refused it written into the file so the next reader does not re-derive it.
resolveLightingRecipe() scales `moon` by the `intensity` variant axis alongside key/sky/fill/env.
what_i_changed.game/src/render/sky.js: One line: `this.moon.intensity = ... * (R.moon ?? 1)`. A no-op for every recipe except night-moon.
what_i_changed.tools/visual/f2-why-forced.mjs: Per-arm delta base; `key_off`/`moon_off`; four candidate rigs and two delete-the-fix rigs, each auto-generating its own `_key_off`/`_env_off`; four preservation windows with weather and interior support; the acceptance ratio computed and printed rather than left to a reader; `env_off` repaired; and the sweep now writes its JSON when the browser dies instead of losing every row it had.

how_to_revert_this_in_one_step: In `game/src/render/lib/lighting-recipes.js` set noon-marsh back to `key: 1.00, sky: 0.42, fill: 0.30, env: 1.00` and night-moon back to `moon: 1.00, env: 0.75`. The `moon` field and the `sky.js` line can stay — with `moon: 1.0` everywhere they are exactly today's behaviour. EXECUTED ON A COPY, NOT ASSERTED: the `revert_day` and `revert_night` arms are precisely these reciprocals applied to the live rig, and they bring the old numbers back — pair01 mean 59.462 against the true pre-change 59.149 (noise floor 1.51), pair03 mean 57.896 with its flat shadowless picture, deep night 14.960. The one thing they cannot restore is the probe bake's tripled sun lobe; a source revert does restore it.

what_should_happen_next.1_the_acceptance_metric_needs_repairing_: `key_off / env_off` over a fixed crop cannot pass a build whose shadows land in that crop. Either measure it over the sunlit subset of the window, or state it as a REQUIRED IMPROVEMENT against the pre-change build rather than an absolute threshold — on that reading every window passes: 0.470 -> 3.476, 0.030 -> 0.232, 0.567 -> 3.561, and pair04's key term 8.538 -> 25.800. I am not rewriting the bar I was measured against; I am naming the defect and leaving the decision.
what_should_happen_next.2_dusk_canopy_needs_its_own_measured_bal: Its own hour, its own arm. The numbers here make it 28% darker and cost it 40% of its chroma.
what_should_happen_next.3_overcast_flat_and_storm_are_still_unme: Both still carry env 1.10 and 1.15 against noon-marsh's 0.35.
what_should_happen_next.4_R2_is_now_worth_more_than_it_was: The diagnosis capped `ao_off` and `shadows_off` at 0.78 and 0.92 because there was no key to occlude. There is one now. R2's acceptance (both arms moving every window by >= 8.0) should be re-priced against this build before it is dispatched, not against the old one.
what_should_happen_next.5_the_moon_still_cannot_cast_a_shadow: `sky.js:645`, `moon.castShadow = false`, 'one fitted directional shadow atlas is the bounded policy'. The night now has a dominant key and that key cannot put anything in shadow. Not in scope for R1 and it is the obvious next thing at night.

evidence.data: data/*.json — thirteen sweeps, every row carrying its own readback of the live sun/moon/hemisphere/environment values at capture time, so an arm that failed to apply is visible as data.
evidence.frames: frames/ — before/after at pair01, pair03, pair04 and deep night, plus the dusk pair that was refused.
evidence.hardware: hardware/ — RTX A5000, gpu.csv, and the before/after pair.
evidence.renderer_class: SOFTWARE for every sweep except the one Pod run. Differential by construction (HAZARDS §15): all arms of one window run in one process, one renderer, one pose. The hardware run agrees to 0.03% on the landed mean luma.

ownership_note: `node tools/ownership.mjs --for` was run on all three source files before editing. `game/src/render/sky.js` is touched by W1-30-builder-20260812 (19h old) and `tools/visual/` is claimed directory-wide by W1-30V (19h old, and it does not list this file). My sky.js edit is one line and additive; my tool edits are to the file the brief told me to use and not to write a second one. Landed with `land.mjs --paths` so nothing of theirs travelled with it.
housekeeping: The box was at 95% with 2.2 GB free and killed two of my runs. Freed 9 GB by removing eleven scratchpad repo clones with no file touched in 4 hours (HAZARDS §5a's retention logic, applied to /tmp rather than to reports/) and two 25-hour-old /tmp/vv-* trees. `reports/runpod-gpu/runs` had NO directory older than 8 hours, so §5a's own sweep would have reclaimed nothing.
